**Probably yes—but only with some difficulty.**

The Moon is a very thin **~4% waning crescent**, just **6.5° above the east-southeastern horizon** and **22.9° from the Sun**. Although the Sun is still **1.3° below the horizon**, civil twilight is already bright, so contrast will be poor. The Moon’s relatively large separation from the Sun helps, and a 4% crescent is ordinarily visible to the unaided eye under clear conditions.

Your main obstacle is its **very low altitude**: atmospheric extinction, haze, and any hills or buildings can easily hide it. Ushuaia’s mountainous horizon may be especially important.

With a clear, unobstructed view toward **azimuth 101.5° (slightly south of due east)**, you would have a **reasonable chance of seeing it**, particularly if you locate it promptly. Binoculars would make it much easier—but wait until the Sun is safely below the horizon and never sweep near a rising Sun.
